BSU Open Science survey results: 2026

61 scientific staff and students who attended the Summer Away Day in 2026 (69% out of 89 staff appearing on the website in July 2026) completed the survey.

Here we summarise how many people reported different levels of “openness” of different aspects of their research.

Later, the results are broken down by BSU research theme and by staff/student category.

A bigger number (0-3) means more open, and the exact definitions of these categories are given below.

Over all research staff and students

Compared to 2025 results (which coincidentally also had 61 responses)

Definitions of categories

Publications
0 I have published written work, but I haven’t made it “open” by any of these standards.
1 All papers open access, and published in relevant repositories, to meet requirements of funders and University.
2 …Most papers also published as preprints when completed, in advance of peer review. If applicable (e.g. clinical trials) analysis protocols are published or studies preregistered.
3 …All papers and completed work published openly in advance of peer review. Smaller pieces of work as online vignettes or blog posts. Continued communication to a range of audiences (e.g. workshops, teaching, social media).
NA Not applicable - I have not published written work
Analysis code
0 I have done analyses of data, but I haven’t made the code “open” by any of these standards.
1 All papers indicate where readers can get the code to reproduce the analysis. Code made openly available online, at least as supplementary material
2 All code made openly available online, e.g. on GitHub, in a concise form matching what is done in the paper, with brief instructions and explanations.
3 … This code is also clearly understandable with minimum effort, made openly accessible via a standard medium (e.g. Github, cloud computing service, web app). Full documentation and explanations, e.g. vignettes, notebooks, clearly integrated with the paper. Use of containerisation if necessary.
NA Not applicable - I have not done analyses of data
Software
0 I have written software, but I haven’t made it “open” by any of these standards.
1 Software made available online (e.g. on GitHub) and referenced in any papers that use it.
2 Software packaged in a standard format, and made available on an established repository (e.g. CRAN, PyPI, GitHub).
3 … This software also has clear and full documentation and worked examples of usage. Some or all of: good error handling, unit testing, continuous integration, issue tracking. Engagement with any users. Software maintained, e.g. to fix bugs and keep up to date with current platforms
NA Not applicable - I have not written software to implement novel methods
Data
0 I have not made my research data “open” by any of these standards
1 All papers include a data availability statement, as required by many journals. Any simulated data, or code to generate it, published online.
2 … In addition, there is documentation for how data were generated, and “metadata” explaining what the data means. If data are not permitted to be shared, then synthetic data are made available with the same structure as the data that were analysed.
3 … In addition, all input and output data are openly available via online repositories, or via data access agreements, as far as legal restrictions allow.
NA Not applicable - I have not used or generated data in research
